enhanced.fullText:
Cafeteria Plan Regulations under Section 125 of the Internal Revenue Code (26 U.S.C. § 125) establish the framework for employer-sponsored benefit plans that allow employees to exclude certain benefits from gross income through pre-tax salary reductions. These regulations, codified in 26 CFR § 1.125-1 through 1.125-8, are particularly significant for higher education institutions offering comprehensive benefit packages to faculty and staff.

Under 26 U.S.C. § 125(a), a cafeteria plan must be a separate written plan that meets specific qualification requirements. The plan allows participants to choose between taxable compensation and qualified benefits including accident and health insurance premiums, group-term life insurance up to $50,000, dependent care assistance up to $5,000 annually, and adoption assistance benefits. For higher education institutions, this creates substantial tax advantages for both employers and employees while managing benefit costs.

Critical limitations apply under 26 U.S.C. § 125(a)(4) and 26 CFR § 1.125-1(q). Qualified scholarships, tuition reduction benefits under Section 117, educational assistance programs under Section 127, and deferred compensation arrangements are explicitly excluded from cafeteria plan treatment. This restriction is particularly relevant for universities that commonly provide tuition benefits to employees and their dependents.

The timing rules under 26 CFR § 1.125-1(c) require that benefits be treated as received in the taxable year when the plan year ends, not when services are rendered or elections made. Universities must carefully coordinate their academic year calendars with cafeteria plan years to ensure proper tax reporting.

Nondiscrimination requirements under 26 U.S.C. § 125(b) and 26 CFR § 1.125-7 prohibit plans from discriminating in favor of highly compensated employees or key employees. Universities must conduct annual nondiscrimination testing, particularly challenging given diverse compensation structures for faculty, administrators, and staff. Failure to satisfy these tests results in includible compensation for highly compensated participants.

Enforcement occurs through IRS audits and employee complaints, with penalties including disqualification of the entire plan, resulting in all participants losing tax-favored treatment. The IRS may also impose excise taxes and require amended payroll tax returns. Recent updates include increased dependent care assistance limits under the American Rescue Plan Act and modified testing requirements under 26 CFR § 1.125-7(c)(3).
enhanced.summary: Cafeteria Plan Regulations under 26 U.S.C. § 125 govern pre-tax employee benefit elections, requiring written plans, nondiscrimination testing, and specific exclusions for educational benefits commonly offered by universities.
enhanced.requirements:
## Plan Documentation Requirements
- Maintain written cafeteria plan document complying with 26 CFR § 1.125-1(c)
- Include specific benefit offerings, election procedures, and plan year definitions
- Update plan documents annually to reflect benefit changes and regulatory updates
- Ensure HR departments maintain current plan documentation

## Nondiscrimination Testing
- Conduct annual testing under 26 U.S.C. § 125(b) by plan year end
- Test participation and benefits for highly compensated employees
- Document testing results and corrective actions if discrimination found
- Benefits administration staff responsible for testing compliance

## Employee Elections and Administration
- Establish annual open enrollment periods with irrevocable elections
- Implement qualified change event procedures under 26 CFR § 1.125-4
- Maintain election records for audit purposes
- Payroll departments ensure proper pre-tax deductions

## Educational Benefit Exclusions
- Exclude tuition reduction benefits from cafeteria plan elections per 26 U.S.C. § 125(a)(4)
- Separate administration of Section 127 educational assistance programs
- Ensure scholarship programs remain outside cafeteria plan structure
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Annual nondiscrimination testing must be completed by plan year end with results documented. Form W-2 reporting of cafeteria plan benefits required by January 31st annually. Quarterly payroll tax returns must reflect proper pre-tax treatment of cafeteria plan elections.
